verdicts.title: 3D: every match leaks its whole renderer, scene, match DOM and match closures (about 3.5 MB of JS heap and 20-40 MB of process memory per match)
verdicts.notes:
REPRODUCED with my own scripts in /tmp/rt/perf-verify/out (worktree at derby/main 623a5a1, dist rebuilt).

SETUP: leak.cjs plays short ranked matches, returns to Home, forces 3x HeapProfiler.collectGarbage, then reads Performance.getMetrics and counts instances with Runtime.queryObjects. Command: NODE_PATH=/opt/node22/lib/node_modules node leak.cjs 3d 4 3.

HARNESS PITFALL I hit first: tests/e2e/lib/helpers.cjs:218 startRanked() calls page.waitForSelector(SEL.pitch). That returns an ElementHandle that is never disposed, and it pins each #pitch canvas. In my first run 2D also showed detached #pitch 1,2,3,4 and nodes 627 to 1351, and the heap snapshot root was 'DevTools console'. After switching to locator.waitFor() the 2D run is flat, so the claim holds that only 3D leaks. Any leak test must avoid page.waitForSelector.

2D, clean (4 matches of 2x3 s): heap 3.12 to 4.36, 4.43, 4.56, 4.57 MB. Listeners stay at 35, with 0 detached canvases and 0 ResizeObservers.

3D, clean:
- Heap 3.12, 9.49, 12.44, 15.54, 18.43 MB.
- Nodes 377, 674, 955, 1258, 1537.
- Listeners 35, 49, 63, 77, 91.
- Canvases 0, 39, 76, 112, 147.
- Detached #pitch canvases and WebGL2RenderingContexts 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.
- ResizeObservers 0, 2, 4, 6, 8.
many.cjs ran 9 straight 3D matches: home heap rose linearly from 9.3 to 33.3 MB (about 3 MB per match) and listeners from 49 to 161. There were no WebGL context warnings, because forceContextLoss frees the GPU context, but the JS and DOM side is still held.

SIZE CORRECTION: the claim of 'about 10 MB per full match' is overstated for the JS heap. leakfull.cjs ran two full-length matches (2x180 s, 428 s and 444 s wall time): home heap went 3.12, then 10.61, then 14.17 MB. That is 3.56 MB per full match, against 3.0 MB at 2x3 s and 3.5 MB at 2x30 s, so it barely depends on match length. The first match's extra ~3 MB is one-time three.js setup cost: the fixed build also sits at 6.1-6.7 MB after match 1.

NATIVE MEMORY IS THE BIGGER COST, which the original report missed. The retained subtree keeps its 2D canvas backing stores. rss.cjs found these retained per match:
- The 2048x1386 grass canvas (stadium.ts:101-104, built at 'high' quality, the default on real GPUs).
- The juice-fx canvas at device pixel size.
- About 35 sprite and texture canvases.
Retained backing per match is 10.4 MB at low quality and 20.0 MB at ?quality=high. On a 390x844 DPR-3 phone context at high quality it is 19.3 MB.
Process RSS per match:
- 1280x800, high quality: renderer 412, 421, 435, 449 MB; GPU 279, 318, 333, 358 MB. That is about 35-40 MB per match combined.
- Phone: renderer 414, 424, 436 MB; GPU 269, 296, 314 MB.

ROOT CAUSE, confirmed by retain.cjs (heap snapshot, BFS over strong edges with WeakMap ephemeron edges excluded):
- Path: GC roots, then a window listener closure, then a module-scope variable (minified `Us`). That variable is three's DFG_LUT DataTexture singleton (vendor/three/three.module.js:16074-16081).
- Then: its _listeners.dispose[i], the onTextureDispose closure added in initTexture (three.module.js:11737), that closure's WebGL2RenderingContext, and finally the detached canvas#pitch.
- With ephemeron edges included, the shortest path instead runs through the shared Sprite geometry's index attribute (the module-level _geometry, three.core.js:22432/22489). Its listener is onGeometryDispose, added at three.module.js:4182.
- WebGLRenderer.dispose (three.module.js:17123) never removes these listeners from shared objects. Renderer3D.dispose (src/client/r3d/renderer3d.ts:729-754) calls gl.dispose() and forceContextLoss() but leaves them in place.
- Once the canvas is pinned, everything hanging off it is pinned too: the detached .pitch-wrap, its listeners, the mountMatch closure in src/client/matchView.ts (Renderer3D, ReplayBuffer, ResizeObservers), and all texture canvases.

FIX VERIFIED. I patched renderer3d.ts dispose() in my scratch worktree, then reverted it; the worktree is clean. Before the cleanup loop the patch captures the shared LUT and the shared Sprite geometry:
  const lut = this.gl.properties.get(this.ball.material).uniforms?.dfgLUT?.value
  const spriteGeo = this.aim.markers[0].geometry
After the players are disposed, it calls lut?.dispose() and spriteGeo?.dispose(). The ball is a MeshStandardMaterial (renderer3d.ts:253), so its uniforms carry dfgLUT.
- Result (3D, 4 matches): heap 3.12, 6.12, 6.31, 6.53, 6.56 MB; listeners flat at 35; 0 detached canvases; 0 retained WebGL contexts; 0 ResizeObservers.
- At high quality: renderer RSS flat at 396-400 MB, GPU RSS 266-300 MB with no upward trend. This is better than the reporter's 'Renderer3D 1,1,1'.
- Both disposals are needed. With only the Sprite fix, or only the LUT fix, the heap still goes 9.5 to 12.5 MB and retained contexts go 1 to 2.
- With the fix, matches 2 and 3 still render correctly: three re-uploads both singletons on the next render, and there were no console errors. See /tmp/rt/perf-verify/out/fixed-match1.png and fixed-match3.png: identical shading, and the player marker, name label and control ring all show.

SUGGESTED FIX:
- In Renderer3D.dispose (src/client/r3d/renderer3d.ts:729), dispose three's module singletons this renderer touched, before this.gl.dispose() at line 751:
  - The DFG LUT, read from the material's uniforms before the ball material is disposed at line 740.
  - The shared Sprite geometry. Expose it from AimLayer (src/client/r3d/aim3d.ts:239 creates the Sprites; dispose is at :490), for example by having AimLayer.dispose call this.markers[0]?.geometry.dispose().
  - Comment that these are three singletons. Disposing them is safe even if another renderer is alive, because it re-uploads.
- The sturdier option is a single long-lived WebGLRenderer and canvas re-parented into each match and the replay viewer. That also saves context creation and shader compiles.
- Add an e2e test in tests/e2e/view.e2e.cjs: play 3 short ?renderer=3d matches, starting each with locator('#pitch').waitFor(), not startRanked's page.waitForSelector. After each, run HeapProfiler.collectGarbage, then assert that JSEventListeners and Nodes stay flat and that Runtime.queryObjects(WebGL2RenderingContext.prototype) returns 0.

UNTESTED: the replay viewer also builds its renderer through createMatchRenderer and probably leaks the same way.

SEVERITY: major stands. Matches are played back to back in one tab, and each one adds about 280 DOM nodes, 14 listeners, about 3.5 MB of JS heap and 20-40 MB of process memory that is never freed. On phones that leads to tab reloads or kills in long sessions.
